title: Data-Centric Diet: Effective Multi-center Dataset Pruning for Medical Image Segmentation
mechanism: Per-sample importance from training dynamics on target regions (Dynamic Average Dice) for multi-centre data; gradient-norm scores fail on segmentation.
adaptation: Compute per-cell crack/inactive Dice across saved checkpoints of existing house runs, per source; low-and-flat cells are noise candidates to cross-check with ensemble ranking.
min_experiment: No training: correlate dynamics score with ensemble ranking and 24 audit cells. Kill: weaker audit agreement than ensemble ranking.
evidence: R: DAD-based pruning beats gradient-norm metrics on combined-source medical segmentation benchmarks (abstract-level evidence).
